meta.title: The Old Town Visitor Line
meta.textType: story: a phone call, with a recorded message and an answer from the office

paragraphs: On Friday, February fifth, at six o'clock in the evening, Lily sat at the kitchen table. Mom's cell phone lay in front of her. "You can use it for one call," said Mom. Lily wanted the facts about the Explorers' walk in the old town on Saturday, February thirteenth. A leaflet from Teacher Kim lay next to the phone. It had the number of the Old Town Visitor Line. Tom sat across from her with a notebook. Pip lay under the table and looked up at them. "The line may be busy," said Tom. "It is only six o'clock," said Lily, "so the office may still be open." She held the phone to her ear and a pencil in her other hand.

A recorded voice answered. "Good evening. This is the Old Town Visitor Line of the Old Town Tour Company. We are a local company, and we welcome every tourist. The walk starts at the old gate at nine o'clock every Saturday and takes two hours. It shows the history of the old town. A child's ticket is twenty baht, and an adult's ticket is forty baht. The office closes at seven o'clock. Press one to talk to the office." Lily said each fact again, and Tom wrote the time, the length, and the prices in his notebook.

Lily pressed one. Then she put the phone on the table and pressed the speaker button, so that Tom could hear. The phone rang twice, and Pip came out from under the table. He sat on the floor and looked at the phone with his head on one side. "Hello, Old Town Visitor Line," said a man. Pip barked loudly. Lily laughed and covered the phone with her hand. Then she took her hand away. "Sorry, that is my puppy," she said. The man laughed, too.

"First, I have two questions," said Lily. "Can you give me directions to the old gate from the bus stop?" "Walk up the street, and you will see the gate on your left," said the man. "Next, is there a toilet?" asked Lily. "Yes, behind the tea shop," said the man. "Look out for the green flag at the gate." "Thank you very much," said Lily. "Have a nice walk!" said the man.

After that, Lily ended the call and looked at Tom. "I am not interested in the old town," said Tom. He wrote "toilet behind tea shop" and "green flag at gate" in his notebook. "Why do you write everything?" asked Lily. "The walk may be long, and it might be hot, so I want to know everything," said Tom. Pip barked once more, and Lily laughed.
text.summary: Lily calls the Old Town Visitor Line from the kitchen to get the facts for the club walk. She hears a recorded message, talks to a man at the office, and Tom writes everything in his notebook.
